title: BRAVENT: fire development and ventilation in schools (SINTEF report 2022:00394), with a described Oslo school fire concept
jurisdiction: Norway. Research report by SINTEF Community for Oslobygg KF; the school case is 'Skole A, Oslo kommune' as named in the report. Comparative only, not Alberta.
code_edition: TEK 17 cited as current minimum requirements (p. 13); VTEK referred to for pre-accepted solutions (p. 15)

facts.text: Report 2022:00394 (open access), version 1.0 dated 2022-10-29; commissioned by Oslobygg KF; keywords include literature study, field investigation and teaching buildings.
Project explores an alternative 'trekk ut' (exhaust) ventilation strategy that relies only on the existing comfort-ventilation system, as an option for older school buildings.

Section 5.1 'Skole A, Oslo kommune' describes the school's fire concept: glazed atrium (Glassgård) smoke vents of 6 m² on level 1; exhaust strategy 'Trekk ut' without fire-insulated ducts or a bypass fan.
Because of sprinklers, fire insulation of ventilation ducts can be omitted. The report calls this a deviation from VTEK, and says the solution is documented.
Section 5.1.2: the school is fully sprinklered to NS EN 12845 and FG rules because of large fire compartments.
States that minimum air-change requirements remain in TEK 17, the current version of the regulation.
Keyword scan found no architectural drawing sheets in the PDF; figures are charts and photographs.

limitations: Comparative test only (Norway, Oslo school). A research report, not a permit application; the school's own fire drawings are not in the PDF.
The report is open access; no redistribution assumed beyond this local research folder.
